coordinateSpace: anchorX/anchorY, advanceWidth/advanceHeight, padding and faceQuad are CSS px of the @1x texture, with a top-left origin. textureFile2x is the same shell at pixelRatio times the resolution; divide its pixels by pixelRatio to get the same coordinates.

shadowContract.note: Phase 1c refinement, variant C: the shadow is darker and still diffuse; it is darkest at the tile and fades over a 20 px falloff. Peak alpha 0.30, contact floor 0.08, 10 px @1x blur, 20 px right/bottom padding, 10-16 px visible extent, 1-2 px top/left AO at 0.20. The shadow/AO are a separate sprite: the runtime draws every shadow first, then every tile body, so a shadow can never sit on top of a neighbouring tile. The window follows the silhouette inside the body box. The check enforces the ranges.

stack.note: A wall column is a stack of two tiles built from the same single shell perspective (Tenhou-style: the perspective does not change down the column even though it physically would). The bottom tier is a face-down wall shell; the top tier is the same shell offset by the published stackStepPx, or the face-up dora shell for a revealed indicator. The stack step is the projected thickness (straight up), not the face grid step.

baseScale.note: Phase 1b decision: the Phase 1 @2x output is the new @1x base. The long axis of the projected tile body is now 104 CSS px at @1x (was 52) and 208 px at @2x, so the board coordinate space doubles in both axes and every consumer must read the new shells.json. Render real pixels at the new resolution; never upscale the Phase 1 textures. The 3-4 px right/bottom shadow and 1-2 px top/left AO contract is unchanged in pixels at the new @1x.

shadow.source: Cycles shadow-catcher alpha, clamped to padding.right/bottom

rig.determinism: CPU Cycles, fixed seed 0, fixed adaptive threshold and OIDN. Each texture records the sha256 of its decoded RGBA; re-baking the same spec must reproduce it (bake_shells.py --bake --verify-determinism renders each shell twice; --audition --verify-determinism does the same for every candidate).
